note: Raw attacker-controlled config input (up to 32768 bytes, filling the fuzzer destination buffer exactly) enters the config parser; the full length is passed as 'len' with no slack byte reserved.

The lexer's end bound is set to the last byte of the input buffer; the vulnerable code does not reserve a terminator byte (the fix passes len-1), so EOF-triggered scanning can step one byte past the destination buffer.
The final input byte is '$' (a fresh token after a linefeed), so lex_config evaluates peek(lexer), which advances the scan position past the end of the buffer.
peek() first calls next(); with pos already at end, next() sets pos = end + 1 and returns '\0', then peek() immediately calls backup().
EOF guard fires because pos has reached end (the last byte of the destination buffer).

Root cause: on EOF the scan position is advanced one byte past the end of the destination buffer without enforcing its bounds; the subsequent backup() then dereferences the byte at index len, which is out of bounds (global-buffer-overflow).

Sink: after lexer->pos--, pos == data+len (one past the 32768-byte destination buffer); the read *lexer->pos is the ASAN-detected global-buffer-overflow READ of size 1 (crash state backup -> peek -> lex_config).
